correctness.rationale: The reduction of UW−V² has q² zeros, with unique singular zero the origin even in characteristic 2 (if U=W=0, the equation forces V=0). For the cubic, the field cases a≠0, a=0 with b≠0, and a=b=0 give respectively (q−1)q³,(q−1)q²,q² zeros. There are q² rank-at-most-one points: with a≠0 choose a,b and use the rank-one relations; with a=0 the minors force b=c=d=0. Each rank-two point has a unit directional derivative by the Schur chart, or by −b² or −d² in the complementary cases. A unit derivative gives a bijection in the chosen coordinate on a fixed residue class: each next-digit change modifies the output by the derivative times that digit, and hence uniquely lifts each preceding solution. This does not assume a coefficient field. At a rank-one residue, a or e is a unit; the invertible Schur coordinate transformation makes the three residual entries uniformly independent in (π) conditional on the residue class and free values of a,b. Multiplication by π bijects R/(π^(m−1)) with (π), so the rank-one quadratic and origin homogeneous recurrences use honest uniform shorter-ring coefficients, with no ignored terminal condition. For shifts of size at least m the whole contribution is already in the terminal bin; otherwise coefficients below m follow by induction using the respective shifts 1,2,3. The rational solutions follow by solving the two recurrences, first for Q and then the cubic. Their finite tails are recovered by subtracting lower coefficients, and the only nearest pole t=u⁻¹ has coefficient 1−u³ when expressed as a multiple of (1−ut)⁻¹. The remaining possible pole moduli are distinct between the two other denominator factors and at least u⁻³ᐟ², giving the asserted summed remainder. Separately, an independent Leibniz enumeration over the ramified characteristic-four ring Z[X]/(X²−2,X³) gives (1/2,3/16,9/64,11/64) at length three. The frozen checker and saved output were inspected, not run.
